producer: Claude implementation agent (build, and the three fix rounds after the reviews); not an independent reviewer

evidence.detail: Rows ac1/after-the-receipt (landed is sent once for the unit by its land dispatch; every event of the landing is sent while the receipt of that unit and dispatch is in the store and the land dispatch's record still says running; the ended record carries the step with the receipt's id; Signal is given the source commit and the new trunk tip from the receipt), ac1/failed-landing-sends-nothing (a land of U2 that started and was refused because the trunk moved: no receipt, no event, nothing written to the ledger, the worktree in git's list with its build output byte for byte, the items present, no space step in the record; its re-land lands and only then is landed sent, the worktree and build output removed, the branch kept, the kept ref at the commit), ac1/no-receipt-no-event (the station's landed step for a dispatch with no receipt, and with another unit's dispatch: nothing sent, nothing written), ac1/undone-landing-sends-nothing (the local trunk put back to the watermark: nothing sent, the worktree, its notes and build output as they were), ac1/no-ledger-sends-nothing (a station with no ledger lands with no space field, no event and no ledger write).

The rows run the land station's own land on a real store with OpenSSH signatures: the lander's disposable candidate, the installed gate, the Landing and its completion receipt, with the project landing locally (VELDO-0235). The space Ledger is a real one on that same store and connection; every event goes through the real Signal, kind registry, probes, removers and keeper, which really delete real linked worktrees and folders made with plain git. The project is in act mode by the owner's own signed command with a real key. The disk, git and the ledger are read after each call. Stand-ins: assumptions 1 to 6.

space310-sent-when-the-landing-starts is the declared falsifier: landed is sent through Signal when the land dispatch is opened; the land of U2 then fails and ac1/failed-landing-sends-nothing finds the worktree gone and is red. Applied once each, noop copy green, mutant copy red on its target rows: space310-sent-when-the-landing-starts reds ac1/failed-landing-sends-nothing, space310-sent-with-the-trunk-put-back reds ac1/undone-landing-sends-nothing.

Fix round rows. f5/space-step-failed (review finding 5): the Signal stand-in raises inside the space step of a real landing; the land dispatch record is ended landed and was already ended when the step failed, no land dispatch is running, the space step has its own record (land-space:<dispatch>) in state failed, joined to the dispatch and the receipt, with what was raised, and nothing was removed. f1/remote-trunk-put-back (finding 1): at the remote destination the station runs its own step with the bare origin trunk put back just before it; the remote answer is read, nothing is sent, nothing is written to the ledger, no ref of either repository changes and nothing is brought. ac1/after-the-receipt now shows every event sent after the dispatch record ended landed and while the space record was running, and Signal given the source commit only.

Fix round, each applied once and seen red: space310-space-step-inside-the-running-window (the step run before the record is ended, as it was) reds f5/space-step-failed; space310-remote-trunk-not-read (the remote side of _trunk_holds takes the candidate for the remote tip) reds f1/remote-trunk-put-back. The declared falsifier space310-sent-when-the-landing-starts was applied again and still reds ac1/failed-landing-sends-nothing.

Rows ac2/worktree-after-build-output (the record's removals at landed hold the build output and then the worktree; both gone from the disk and removed in the ledger; git lists no such worktree; the method is keep_then_git_worktree_remove; the keep step was called for the worktree and the kept ref is in the main repository at its commit), ac2/branch-kept-and-marked (refs/heads/build/<unit> resolves to the evidence commit, the branch item is kept, the record names it marked with its ref, tip and event; every planted branch of the repository still resolves), ac2/image-tags-go (the unit's image tag is removed in the ledger and from the engine by image rm on the tag, with no force option), ac2/record-joined-to-receipt (the land dispatch's record names the receipt, the new trunk tip, the source and the scope; each removal record in the ledger names the receipt and the landing station as emitter; the station observed the step; the record is under 20000 bytes), ac2/unlanded-work-stays (U3, built on after its evidence commit: the landing is a fact with its receipt, landed is not sent, reason not_landed, the worktree, the later commit and the build output are there with their items present, and the record names the branch and the worktree as left), ac2/uncommitted-work-stays (U4, whose worktree holds an untracked file: the build output is removed, the worktree deferred as unique_work with the file byte for byte, the branch kept at its commit, the record names the deferral).

The rows run the land station's own land on a real store with OpenSSH signatures: the lander's disposable candidate, the installed gate, the Landing and its completion receipt, with the project landing locally (VELDO-0235). The space Ledger is a real one on that same store and connection; every event goes through the real Signal, kind registry, probes, removers and keeper, which really delete real linked worktrees and folders made with plain git. The project is in act mode by the owner's own signed command with a real key. The disk, git and the ledger are read after each call. Stand-ins: assumptions 1 to 6.

space310-branch-removed-with-the-worktree is the declared falsifier: the landing deletes the ref of each branch the event was sent for; ac2/branch-kept-and-marked finds no branch and is red. Applied once each, noop copy green, mutant copy red on its target rows: space310-branch-removed-with-the-worktree reds ac2/branch-kept-and-marked, space310-landed-for-a-branch-built-on reds ac2/unlanded-work-stays.

Fix round rows. f1/remote-unit-landed (finding 1): after a landing at the remote, with no branch, tag or remote-tracking ref of the project repository holding the candidate, the unit branch counts as landed through the source commit; its build output and then its worktree are removed after the keep step (kept ref at the source commit), the branch kept. f4/squash-landing (finding 4): the trunk at a squash commit made with plain git that does not contain the branch commit, a stand-in receipt naming it; landed through the source commit, removed after the keep step, branch kept and marked. f4/one-landed-one-unlanded: a unit with a second branch the landing does not hold, not the first of its branch items; landed is not sent, the record names that branch only, the worktree and both branches are as they were. f4/detached-worktree-at-landed: a detached worktree of the unit at the source commit counts as landed and is removed by the rules and the tool after the keep step.

Fix round, each applied once and seen red: space310-source-commit-not-counted reds f4/squash-landing; space310-first-branch-judged-alone reds f4/one-landed-one-unlanded; space310-detached-refused-at-landed reds f4/detached-worktree-at-landed. The declared falsifier space310-branch-removed-with-the-worktree was applied again and still reds ac2/branch-kept-and-marked.

Rows, every branch planted before the first landing under a ticket of its own: ac3/contained-worktree-removed (a branch moved from its start commit to a commit the new trunk tip contains: contained sent once for its owner, build output then worktree removed, the branch kept in the repository and named marked, the kept ref at the commit), ac3/fresh-branch-left (a worktree on a new branch whose tip is its start commit, which the trunk contains: nothing sent, worktree, build output and items as they were, after the first and the second landing; the record counts it at_start), ac3/no-start-left (a branch recorded with no start commit), ac3/not-in-trunk-left (a branch with a commit the trunk does not hold), ac3/work-in-contained-worktree-stays (a contained branch whose worktree holds an untracked file: deferred as unique_work with the file byte for byte, retried at the second landing and deferred again, attempts 2), ac3/not-alone-left (one ticket with a contained branch and one that is not: nothing sent for that owner at either landing, both worktrees present, the record names the contained branch left as not_alone), ac3/moved-after-the-check (the branch gains a commit between the landing's check and Signal: the worktree is deferred as unique_work and holds the commit, the record names the branch moved and not marked), ac3/other-project-untouched (a branch and worktree of another project in act mode: nothing sent, as they were after every landing), ac3/marked-once (the branch marked at the first landing is not sent the event at the second).

The rows run the land station's own land on a real store with OpenSSH signatures: the lander's disposable candidate, the installed gate, the Landing and its completion receipt, with the project landing locally (VELDO-0235). The space Ledger is a real one on that same store and connection; every event goes through the real Signal, kind registry, probes, removers and keeper, which really delete real linked worktrees and folders made with plain git. The project is in act mode by the owner's own signed command with a real key. The disk, git and the ledger are read after each call. Stand-ins: assumptions 1 to 6.

space310-start-commit-test-dropped is the declared falsifier: the test that the tip is not the start commit is dropped; contained is sent for the fresh branch's owner and ac3/fresh-branch-left is red. Applied once each, noop copy green, mutant copy red on its target rows: space310-start-commit-test-dropped reds ac3/fresh-branch-left, space310-no-start-taken-for-contained reds ac3/no-start-left, space310-not-in-trunk-taken-for-contained reds ac3/not-in-trunk-left, space310-contained-for-an-owner-not-alone reds ac3/not-alone-left, space310-moved-branch-named-marked reds ac3/moved-after-the-check, space310-marked-branch-sent-again reds ac3/marked-once.

Fix round rows. f1/remote-branch-contained (finding 1, AC3 at the remote destination, the default): another branch of the project repository that the remote new tip contains, past its start commit, is contained, its worktree removed after the keep step, the branch kept and marked; a branch recorded in a second repository that held nothing of the landing is contained after the candidate objects were brought into it from the landing clone, with no ref written there (its refs are exactly those before, at the first event and after the step), nothing fetched and no ref holding the candidate. f2/trunk-read-at-the-attempt (finding 2): a clean worktree whose commit only the trunk holds counts as contained at the check; the trunk is put back inside the Signal stand-in; rule 5, given the source commit only, reads the trunk itself and defers the worktree as unique_work, on the disk, its branch at its commit.

Fix round, each applied once and seen red: space310-candidate-not-brought and space310-transfer-writes-a-ref red f1/remote-branch-contained (the second is the owner rule that the transfer writes no ref); space310-candidate-given-to-rule-5 reds f2/trunk-read-at-the-attempt. The declared falsifier space310-start-commit-test-dropped was applied again and still reds ac3/fresh-branch-left.

Fix round 2 row (the re-review's note 3 and its case 3). f1/project-repository-brought: a unit lands at the remote with the lander's workspace discard disabled (it is asked and does nothing; the workspace is still on disk), so no kept ref gives the project's own repository the candidate: when the step begins that repository does not hold it, by a ref or by an alternate. The step copies the candidate's objects from the landing's clone into it and the record names it copied; the refs of that repository at the first event are exactly those before the step, nothing was fetched, and after the step no ref of it holds the candidate. Landed is sent for the unit, with the source commit only, its build output and then its worktree removed after the keep step and its branch kept. Contained still holds: another branch of that repository, which the remote's new tip contains past its start commit, is sent contained once, its worktree removed after the keep step, the branch kept at its commit and named marked.

Fix round 2, applied once and seen red: space310-project-repository-left-to-the-discard (a repository that has kept refs is not brought to) reds f1/project-repository-brought and no other behaviour row: the record names the project's repository not_brought. space310-candidate-not-brought and space310-transfer-writes-a-ref, applied again, are red on this row and on f1/remote-branch-contained.

Fix round 3 rows (finding 3 closed: the events name the items judged, at the versions read). f3/declared-after-the-check, the reviewer's case: an owner's branch, past its start commit and in the new trunk tip, is judged contained with its worktree and build output; inside the Signal stand-in, after the check and before the ledger's command, a fresh worktree is declared and confirmed for the same owner on a new branch at its start commit, clean and in the trunk, which rule 5 would let go. Contained is sent once and names exactly the three items judged, each at the version read at the check. The fresh worktree is not named and is never reached: it, its build output and its branch are on disk and present. The judged items are ended as judged: the build output and then the worktree removed after the keep step, the branch kept at its commit and named marked. f3/changed-after-the-check: for another owner, inside the stand-in the judged worktree is switched to a new branch at its start commit and the switch recorded (rebranch), so its item is at a later version. The ledger refuses the whole event, space_item_version:<the worktree>; the record's event entry is not ok with that reason and the branch is named as left, refused; the worktree, its build output and both branches are on disk and present, the two items that did not change at the version read. A later check judges both owners as they are then: each has a worktree on a branch at its start commit, so contained is not sent (not_alone) and everything is as it was.

Fix round 3, each applied by hand to the copy the suite loads and seen red on its target row: space310-owner-signalled-after-the-check (the owner is signalled, as it was) reds f3/declared-after-the-check, the fresh worktree is removed and its branch kept; space310-refused-event-sent-for-the-owner (an event the ledger refused whole is sent again for the owner) reds f3/changed-after-the-check, the switched worktree and its build output are removed.

checks.name: gate
checks.command: ./scripts/verify.sh was not run by the builder: the lead runs it, the heavy suites and the teeth run through the gate lock.

assumptions: 1. THE CREATORS AND THE HOOKS DECLARE NOTHING YET (VELDO-0302 and VELDO-0311 are not built). The suite declares and confirms each worktree, branch, build output and image tag item itself, with the branch name and the start commit the hooks will record. In production nothing records them yet, so a landing's space step finds no item and sends nothing.

2. NOTHING IN THE ENGINE BUILDS `space` YET. control_service.py builds the station and is outside this footprint: no installation gives the station a ledger, so until that wiring lands every landing runs as before. The suite gives the station the mapping itself. NOT PROVEN HERE: the wiring.

3. THE TWO CHECKS OF A SWITCH TO ACT (VELDO-0332 and 0339) are stand-ins that allow. The project is put in act mode by the owner's signed command; no row runs in report mode, where Signal leaves every item due (VELDO-0331's own suite).

4. THE DOCKER CLIENT is a function holding one image, and THE PROCESS TABLE an empty folder shaped as the kernel's. The units, the floor handoffs and the project records are fixture records and the authority's candidate policy accepts, as in VELDO-0235's suite.

5. THE REMOTE DESTINATION IS DRIVEN NOW (fix round, review finding 1). One unit lands at the bare origin through the publication clone, and the read of the remote trunk (Landing._remote_tip, through the identity wire) is driven by a row and a falsifier. FOUND BY THE ROWS: when the step begins the project repository already holds the candidate, on the kept ref the lander writes when it discards its candidate workspace (VELDO-0303), so AC3 already held for a branch of the project repository; the object transfer is what makes it hold for a repository without that kept ref, and the row drives it with a branch recorded in a second repository. NOT PROVEN: a remote another factory moved on to a commit the publication clone does not hold (nothing is sent then).

6. MARKED CONTAINED is the branch item's outcome kept with the action mark_contained, written by Signal through the ledger, and the landing's own record names the branch. The ledger's item has no field for the mark (control_space.py is outside this footprint).

7. THE LEDGER'S SIGNAL NAMES AN OWNER, NOT AN ITEM. Landed and contained are therefore sent per owner and only when everything the event would reach is landed or contained; an owner with a branch that is not is sent nothing. Design section 5's switched worktree (mark X, leave the worktree on Y, one ticket) leaves X unmarked here. Recorded in the spec's History for the lead. SINCE FIX ROUND 3 the events name items (the ledger's signal that names items, VELDO-0312): each event is sent for exactly the items its check judged, at the versions read. What is judged is unchanged: still once for each owner, and only when the owner has nothing the event ends that is not landed or contained, so the switched worktree's branch X is still left unmarked. Recorded for the lead.
8. ./scripts/verify.sh, the heavy suites and the teeth run were not run by the builder.

9. THE SQUASH LANDING HAS A STAND-IN RECEIPT (fix round, finding 4). The lander makes no squash, so f4/squash-landing gives Landing.receipt a stand-in for one unit that names a squash commit made with plain git as the candidate and the branch commit as the source, and moves the trunk to that commit. The trunk read, the branch reads, Signal, rule 5, the keep step and the remover are the real ones.

10. CLOSED IN FIX ROUND 3 (finding 3). The landing judged a snapshot of the ledger's items and the ledger matched again at the send, so an item declared for the same owner in between was reached though never judged. Now each event names the items judged, at the versions read with the check: an item declared after the check is never reached (row f3/declared-after-the-check), and a judged item that changed refuses the whole event (row f3/changed-after-the-check).

11. A FAILED OR INTERRUPTED SPACE STEP IS NOT RETRIED (finding 5). The land dispatch is ended landed first; the space step record stays failed, or running when the process died in it, and the worktrees end at a later event or by reconcile (VELDO-0315). f5/space-step-failed drives a step that raises; a process that dies in the step is not driven, and by the same order it leaves the dispatch record ended.

12. THE OBJECT TRANSFER WRITES LOOSE OBJECTS NO REF HOLDS into the branch repository. They cost space until that repository collects them, and they are needed only for the reads of that step. Nothing is fetched, no ref is written and nothing is removed by it.

13. A SPACE STEP THAT HANGS, OR A PROCESS THAT DIES BEFORE THE STEP'S RECORD IS OPENED, LEAVES NO READABLE RECORD (fix round 2, the re-review's note 4). A hung step leaves its record running for good and is never run again; a death between the end of the dispatch's record and the open of the step's leaves no space record; and the station's status lists dispatch records only. No work is lost: the landing and its receipt are facts and every worktree and branch stays as it was. It is picked up by VELDO-0315 reconcile, not built. Recorded in the spec's History.

14. A REFUSED EVENT IS NOT SENT AGAIN AT THAT LANDING (fix round 3). When a judged item changed after the check the ledger refuses the whole event and the landing sends nothing in its place; the record names the branches as left, refused. They are judged again at a later landing's check, or by reconcile (VELDO-0315). It costs space until then, never work.

15. NO ALLOWANCE WAS ADDED TO THE LEDGER (fix round 3). The station's ledger commands are sent as the installation wires them; the ledger's rule for who may sign limits the two host principals only, and the runner stays refused for a signal that names items (suite 149, r2/runner-names-no-items).

16. THE REGISTERED FALSIFIER SET WAS RUN, 2026-11-14 (no code of this ticket changed since its last fix round; control_launch.py and control_clone.py changed under VELDO-0308 fix 4). python3 scripts/check_teeth_mutations.py --finding 310, run under nice -n 10 on the tree of commit 353a60eb (clean), with a stub engine that was never called and no cargo involved: mutations: passed registered=21 executed=21 reused=0 rejected=21. A first run of this set in the same round rejected every case too but its stage was void (driver_error: inputs changed during stage): the builder edited and committed other files in the worktree while it ran. The count recorded is the second run's, on the still tree. The gate (./scripts/verify.sh) was not run.
rollback: Revert the change. A landing removes nothing, and the worktrees of landed branches stay until another event ends them.
